newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan police detain cult leader for fraud.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan police detain cult leader for fraud.

text.p: A cult leader in Taiwan accused of swindling followers out of T$3 billion (US$109 million) appeared in public on Sunday reaffirming his divine origins and was immediately arrested.
Sung Chi-yi, who went to ground after the allegations on October 9, appeared at a news conference to announce he was the reincarnation of a cosmic body with a ubiquitous soul.
He was detained by police after the news conference at which he denied charges of corruption but refused to demonstrate his supposed special powers.
"I am not a clown or (magician) David Copperfield, so why should I perform?" Sung, dressed in a formal business suit, said.
"If you can't see my miracles, it is only that you haven't opened your heart and mind," he said to thunderous applause from fervent supporters.

Some followers, thought to number thousands across Taiwan, wept openly as Taipei authorities on Sunday dismantled the "Sung Chi-li Memorial", the cult's centre, for operating without a proper licence.
Several of Sung's former followers have accused him of defrauding T$3 billion from cult members by convincing them he has miracle-healing and other supernatural powers.
A photographer admitted last Friday that he had faked pictures showing Sung with a halo around his head.
Sung himself became the fifth person detained from his "Sung Chi-li Association" in what police suspect was a major fraud ring possibly involving top officials and businessmen.

Frank Hsieh, vice presidential candidate for the main opposition Democratic Progressive Party in this year's March election, has been accused of belonging to and receiving donations from the association. He has denied any wrongdoing but admitted that he served as Sung's legal attorney.
Local media reports also have linked Taiwan's vice police chief Yu Yu-tang to Sung's association. Yu has said he knew of Sung, but did not know anything about the operation in Sung's association.
No charges have been filed so far in the case and prosecutors refused to comment on Sunday.
